# Alcántara - TV Broadcast Overlay Control System

A professional TV broadcast overlay control system built with a modern tech stack.

Alcantara also owns the versioned public-destination decision for each explicit
television Start. The command always follows Alcantara → Alana → Croccante;
only Croccante resolves stream-key-bearing Secrets Manager values. See
[`docs/broadcast-destinations.md`](docs/broadcast-destinations.md) for the
catalog, permission, immutable selection, recovery, and redaction contracts.

## Tech Stack

- **Frontend**: React Router v7 + Vite + Tailwind CSS
- **Backend**: NestJS + Fastify + Prisma
- **Database**: PostgreSQL
- **Monorepo**: pnpm workspace

### Six-guest WebRTC contribution

The Calls console at `/calls` provides six reusable guest slots. An operator
with `alcantara:webrtc:operate` can create a persisted private invitation,
choose its one-to-seven-day lifetime (24 hours by default), copy it, replace or
revoke it, remove its current session, and select the guest's Program, Preview,
or no return video plus Program/Master, monitor, or Aux 1-8 return audio.
Invitation secrets are shown only at creation/replacement; the database stores
only their SHA-256 hash. Guest and operator LiveKit credentials expire after
five minutes and are scoped to one program room. The LiveKit API secret never
enters either browser.

Guests enter `/guest/:invitation` without Cognito, select devices, preview their
camera, test their speaker/network, and confirm headphones before explicitly
joining. A documented acoustic-risk override is available when headphones are
impossible. Each invitation permits one active browser session. A signed
session lease refreshed every 20 seconds preserves the stable slot for a
60-second network-reconnect window; a second browser fails closed. Revocation
disconnects the guest and prevents future credentials. A join refused as
revoked, expired or invalid (401 or 403) ends the guest's session; any other
refusal (the invitation in use in another window, the studio not ready, a
network or room-connection failure) keeps the preflight and lets the guest
press Join again. A refused camera or microphone permission keeps Join locked.

Operator mute is immediate. Camera/microphone enable is delivered as a request
that the guest accepts or rejects. Standby/live/wrap cues and private messages
persist requested, delivered, acknowledged/read, rejected, or failed state. A
message is marked read as soon as the guest's page shows it and stays on screen
until the guest presses Acknowledge, so operators see read and then
acknowledged.
Private talkback publishes only to the target guest's N-1 route and never to the
Program feed. Removing or disconnecting a guest does not mutate Preview or
Program.

Layouts use the `webrtc-guest` component with a generic slot number from 1-6,
not a person or invitation identifier. Assigning a replacement invitation to
the same slot therefore preserves reusable layouts. The normal Preview, CUT,
and TAKE workflow remains the only way a guest reaches air.

#### Return routing

Alana remains the owner of captured Program/Preview output publication. Start
its Program renderer with `?renderer=1` so guest microphones are excluded from
the captured base bus, and publish the output to the matching
`alcantara-<programId>` LiveKit room as `program-feed-<programId>` (and optional
`preview-feed-<programId>`). Run one isolated
`/return-router/<programId>#key=<WEBRTC_RENDERER_KEY>` renderer alongside it.
The fragment is immediately moved to session storage and removed from browser
history; it is never sent in a URL request.

The return router subscribes to the selected processed base bus, connected
guest microphones, and targeted producer talkback. It creates and publishes a
distinct Web Audio destination for every guest, excluding only that guest's
own microphone. Guests subscribe only to their selected video output and their
own `mixminus:<identity>:<bus>` track. This replaces the earlier fixed 250 ms
browser relay and keeps isolated guest tracks out of the guest UI.

Authorized operators can control Alana's independent composed-Program recorder
without treating a requested or finalizing operation as safe media. See
[`docs/program-recording.md`](docs/program-recording.md) for the pinned Alana
contract, state semantics, permissions, idempotency, local fixture, private
configuration, metrics, and recovery boundary.

#### Local and production operations

The production backend also writes a verified, encrypted logical PostgreSQL
backup to the media bucket at the top of every UTC hour. See
[`docs/production-database-backups.md`](docs/production-database-backups.md) for
the recovery boundary, storage path, telemetry, and post-deployment checks.

`docker compose up --build` includes LiveKit 1.13.4 with fixed local-only
credentials and TCP/UDP media ports. Alcantara continues to use its existing
database and Pompeii authorization configuration; this stack does not start a
second Pompeii service. From `/calls`, create six fictional guest
links and open them in separate browser contexts. Chrome's fake-device flags
may be used for repeatable automated media UAT. Verify all six show as connected
without appearing on Preview/Program, assign slots to a reusable layout, then
exercise Preview and TAKE deliberately. Restart one guest and verify its slot
is held for 60 seconds. The machine-only return router requires the local
`WEBRTC_RENDERER_KEY` from Compose.

Production owns LiveKit, Redis, TLS, TURN/TLS, firewall rules, health checks,
and secrets through Alcantara deployment infrastructure. Start from
`infra/livekit.production.example.yaml`, generate real API/session/renderer
secrets in the application-scoped secret. Route public LiveKit HTTPS/WSS through
the existing port-443 edge, and expose WebRTC TCP 7881, TURN/TLS 5349, TURN UDP
3478, and the configured UDP media/relay ranges. Validate TURN
from a restrictive external network before scheduling remote guests. Never use
the committed local credentials outside Compose. The Calls console reports the
feature as unavailable until `LIVEKIT_CONFIG_B64`, `LIVEKIT_API_KEY`,
`LIVEKIT_API_SECRET`, `WEBRTC_SESSION_SECRET`, `WEBRTC_RENDERER_KEY`, and the
public `LIVEKIT_WS_URL` deployment variable are configured; their absence does
not block unrelated Alcantara deployments.

### Radio automation

Continuous filler rotation, optional timed content blocks, per-cue browser voice tracks, output confidence, and a prepared Palazzo recovery playlist are documented in [`docs/radio-station-workflow.md`](docs/radio-station-workflow.md).

Radio song sequences default to autoplay when their mode is absent. An explicit
operator choice of Manual remains authoritative. In autoplay, Alcantara advances
to the next playlist item only after Palazzo reports that the active track ended;
looped playlists wrap to the first item and non-looped playlists stop at the end.
Shuffle persists and displays a randomized no-repeat order, advances through it
on the same authoritative Palazzo end events, and wraps only when Loop is on.
Play Next is a separate persisted FIFO queue of playlist references. It never
interrupts the current track. At the next authoritative track end it takes
priority, then Autoplay or Shuffle resumes from the playlist successor that
would have played; Manual remains stopped after the queue drains.
Up to 12 playlist songs can be starred for High Rotation. Automatic playback
opens one High Rotation opportunity every 30 minutes, chooses the least
recently played eligible favorite, and persists authoritative starts across
restarts. The 48 daily opportunities are distributed evenly across the current
favorites, guaranteeing at least four plays per favorite per day: 12 favorites
play four times each, while four favorites play 12 times each. The repeat gap
scales with the pool (`favorite count / 2` hours), avoiding repeats until every
other favorite has had its opportunity. Play Next remains the explicit
operator override, and any queued favorite play counts when choosing the least
recently played song.
The playback bar exposes pressed states for Manual, Autoplay, Shuffle, and Loop
and labels backend playback feedback as live or stale.

The Radio desk includes live Song, Audio clips / bumpers, and Main mixer
controls. Playlist rows can be starred for High Rotation or added to Play Next
without changing playlist order, and the queue supports removal and ordering
before playback. Radio
distribution at `/radio-settings` owns Palazzo automation,
bumper policy, and now-playing consumers so live playout is not mixed with
configuration. Simulcast uses the TV switcher with an explicit radio-leg status
rail. Mixer mutations are applied to Palazzo as well as persisted; bumper
configuration fields are validated and saved by the radio settings API.
All Palazzo traffic is backend-only, restricted to the private broadcast
network and approved origin, and explicitly program-scoped. The shared machine
client preserves playback/idempotency IDs across retries and is also used by
telemetry reconnect and startup recovery.
See [`docs/radio-telemetry.md`](docs/radio-telemetry.md) for the contract,
Secrets Manager bootstrap, allowlisted URLs, failure behavior, and metrics.

### Program output

Alcantara is the program control plane. A program can reference an immutable
template manifest published by Cronkite; the operator UI opens that external
renderer with the program ID and Alcantara API origin from the manifest's
runtime-parameter contract. The legacy `/program/:programId` renderer remains
only as a temporary rollback path until the Fifthbell registration and live
cutover have been verified. See
[Program template contracts](docs/program-templates.md) for registration,
security, state/SSE projection, metrics, and removal gates.

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites

- Docker & Docker Compose

### AWS infrastructure ownership

Macondo provisions the shared Cumulus host, network, and Arauco database. The
service-specific AWS integration lives in [`infra/aws`](infra/aws): Alcántara
owns its GitHub OIDC deployment role, API DNS record, and the policies granting
the Cumulus host access to media storage. Macondo grants its instance
role access to every database secret it provisions; the backend resolves
Arauco credentials inside the container through that instance profile.

### Development

#### Option 1: Using Docker Compose (recommended)

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

This starts PostgreSQL, applies every committed migration non-interactively,
loads deterministic fictional data, and starts the backend, frontend, and
LiveKit. No AWS or Cognito account is needed for local development. Ports are
configurable via `.env`:

- **Backend** (NestJS, default port 3000) with hot reload via `nest start --watch`
- **Frontend** (React Router/Vite, default port 5173) with HMR
- **Broadcast destinations** (`/broadcasts`) with two fictional, version-pinned
  local catalog entries. This exercises the normal API, authorization guards,
  PostgreSQL snapshots, and Alana client boundary.
- **Alana contract fixture** on the private Compose network, used only for local
  destination reload/Start/Stop exercises. It validates authentication,
  sequencing, and exact selection acknowledgement without AWS or public output;
  it is not a deployment or a substitute for production Alana/Croccante proof.

Source directories are mounted so changes are reflected immediately.

The local stack never reaches real AWS or another real outside service
(gaulatti/alcantara#206):

- **Media store.** Uploads, song and artwork playback, radio recovery audio and
  filler digests use a localstack S3 (`localstack/localstack:4.0.3`, port
  `LOCALSTACK_PORT`, default 4566) with the bucket `alcantara-local-only`,
  created by `infra/localstack-init/01-bucket.sh`. Objects are served at
  `http://localstack.localhost:4566/alcantara-local-only/…`, which the browser
  and the backend both resolve to the host's published port.
- **Credentials.** Compose overrides every AWS name `backend/.env` could hold
  with local placeholders or empty values, does not mount `~/.aws`, and empties
  `ARAUCO_SECRET_ID`, so no Secrets Manager secret is read. The frontend gets
  empty `VITE_COGNITO_*` and `VITE_FQDN`; TEST AUTH needs none of them.
- **Start-up refusal.** Outside production the backend refuses to start when
  `MEDIA_S3_BUCKET` is set without `MEDIA_S3_ENDPOINT`, or when
  `MEDIA_S3_ENDPOINT` or `LOCAL_MEDIA_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` points anywhere but a
  local host (loopback, `*.localhost` or a Compose service name). Production
  refuses to start with either of those two variables set. Each error names the
  variable, never its value.
- **Now-playing and charts.** Outside production no now-playing consumer is
  contacted (Radio settings says so, and the backend logs how many were
  skipped), and the two third-party chart feeds are not polled.
- **Check.** `scripts/check-compose-local.sh` confirms from
  `docker compose config` that every one of these names resolves to its local
  value, without printing any value.

This README is the only description of the local media store; the repository
wiki has no page for it yet.

Local browser authentication is visibly marked `TEST AUTH`. It uses short-lived
tokens with a local-only issuer and these deterministic identities:

- `operator-a` (default) and `operator-b`: normal operator permissions
- `viewer`: read-only, including denial of shared-layout publication

For visual review of the shared login shell, append `?auth-state=` to `/login`
while running the frontend in development. Supported fixtures are `loading`,
`ready`, `submitting`, `failure`, and `authenticated`; production builds ignore
the parameter. The authenticated fixture holds the visible redirect state for
inspection, while a real authenticated session continues immediately to `/`.

Choose an identity before starting or recreating the frontend:

```bash
TEST_AUTH_IDENTITY=viewer docker compose up --build
```

Re-running the backend seed restores deterministic profiles, console presets,
and TV, Radio, and Simulcast workflow fixtures without creating duplicates:

```bash
docker compose exec backend pnpm seed
```

To deliberately erase the disposable local database and replay migrations and
seed data from an empty volume:

```bash
docker compose down -v
docker compose up --build
```

The `postgres-data` volume otherwise preserves local changes across restarts.
`AUTH_MODE=test` fails startup under `NODE_ENV=production`; the issuance route
is absent when test auth is disabled, and test tokens use a distinct issuer and
audience that production verification does not accept.

The backend uses the code-owned `host.docker.internal:50087` endpoint while
developing in Compose and the code-owned `api.pompeii.gaulatti.com:443` TLS
endpoint in production with Gaulatti team `1`; no Pompeii endpoint variable is
required.
The browser attaches its current Cognito ID token to every request targeting
Alcantara's configured API origin; requests to external media and data sources
remain unchanged. A backend `401` triggers one forced Cognito session refresh;
if the refreshed request is still unauthorized, Alcantara clears the persisted
browser identity and returns the operator to login.

## Identity

Alcantara authorizes through Pompeii, which now returns a canonical
`principal_id` alongside the pool subject. Operator preferences, shared console
layouts, guest invitations, and guest lifecycle audit events record it beside
the subject through nullable/additive references; ownership matches the
canonical principal when a row names one and falls back to the pool subject when
it does not, so migrated and unmigrated rows both work during rollout.

Identities are never joined by email, no ownership row changes without a verified
Pompeii mapping, and audit attribution is never rewritten. See
[`docs/canonical-principals.md`](docs/canonical-principals.md) for the inventory,
the dry-run report, and the rollback and reconciliation procedure.

The API accepts only interactive session tokens. The authorization guard
answers `401` with `{"error":"UNAUTHENTICATED","reason":"DENY_UNSUPPORTED_CREDENTIAL"}`
for a bearer whose credential starts with `pmp_pat_` (bare or after a `Bearer`
scheme in any letter case), before any authorization call, and counts it in
`alcantara_auth_refusals_total{reason="unsupported_credential"}`. Every other
bearer is handled exactly as before.

Authorization decisions use one long-lived gRPC channel to Pompeii. A Pompeii
deploy replaces its container, and a connection through the old path can stop
carrying bytes without an error, so calls on it only time out. When an
authorization call ends in `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` or `UNAVAILABLE`, the backend
replaces the channel (each channel has its own subchannel pool, so the
replacement dials a new connection) and the next call reaches the live Pompeii.
The failed call still answers `503` with
`{"error":"AUTHORIZATION_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE"}`; nothing is allowed on a
failure. Replacements happen at most once every 5 seconds, so a Pompeii slower
than the deadline is not redialled on every request. Each replacement logs
`Pompeii channel replaced after <reason>` and counts
`alcantara_pompeii_channel_resets_total{reason="deadline_exceeded"|"unavailable"}`
(gaulatti/alcantara#225).

## Architecture

- [Access](docs/access.md) is the page where a signed-in person manages their tokens and, with `alcantara:access:manage`, the token switch and grants; [Access: backend, configuration and metrics](docs/access-api.md) documents its `/access` routes, the optional `POMPEII_ACCESS_CREDENTIAL` secret and `alcantara_access_requests_total`.
- [MCP endpoint](docs/mcp.md) documents `/mcp`, its OAuth discovery documents, who can reach it, and the registered tools.
- [External source registry](docs/external-source-registry.md) documents stable source identity, encrypted transport configuration, SSRF controls, one-time credentials, quotas, lifecycle, and metrics.

Production places the backend on the external `broadcast-control` Docker
network shared with Palazzo and Alana. Before stopping the live backend,
deployment runs
a side-effect-free runtime preflight in the new image to resolve and validate
the approved Palazzo URL and the remaining private-service configuration. The
previous container is retained until the replacement passes its startup check
and is automatically restored if the replacement fails. This keeps the existing
radio controller alive when a configuration or startup defect reaches
deployment. On the Cumulus host, deployment removes only Docker images not
referenced by any running or stopped container before pulling a release and
again after retiring the healthy predecessor. This bounds disk use without
removing the live or rollback image.

Production backend stdout and stderr remain available through `docker logs`,
using Docker's host-local `local` driver with a 10 MiB maximum per file and
three retained files. Alcantara does not require a CloudWatch Logs group or
write grant to start, restart, or roll back. See
[Production backend logging](docs/production-backend-logging.md) for validation
and rollback procedures.

The replacement joins `broadcast-control` so the private
`http://palazzo:3100` program-scoped machine API remains resolvable. Production
uses the code-owned `broadcast/production/config` Secrets Manager payload,
including Alana's private recording control URL and token and the external-source
encryption keyring. The deployment workflow validates that payload without
printing it before image build or push. During migration, deployment also
requires the running Palazzo container on the private `broadcast-control`
network. Palazzo does not require an application credential on this single-host,
single-program boundary. Preflight fails without replacing the live backend
when required configuration is unavailable or invalid.

### Data Flow

```
Control Panel → REST API → Database → SSE Broadcast → Program Page
      │                       ↓
      └── Recording API → private Alana control → composed capture state
                         Program State Update
```

1. Control page sends scene activation/chyron update via REST
2. Backend saves to database
3. Backend broadcasts update via SSE
4. Program page receives SSE event and updates display

### SSE Auto-Reconnect

The frontend SSE client automatically reconnects with a 3-second interval if the connection is lost.

# Alcantara review contract

Alcantara is a TV and radio broadcast control system. A NestJS/Fastify/Prisma
backend (PostgreSQL) owns programs, scenes, layouts, flights, the song and
instant library, radio automation driven by authoritative Palazzo playback
telemetry, LiveKit WebRTC contribution, managed external sources, versioned
broadcast-destination selection (Alcantara to Alana to Croccante) and program
recording. A React Router frontend operates it, and a small CDK package
(`infra/aws`) describes its AWS deployment role infrastructure.

Preserve program isolation, the authentication and authorization boundary,
durable idempotency before audible or public effects, bounded dependency
retries, bounded metric labels (controlled enums and normalized routes only),
and the guarantee that stream keys, signed URLs, tokens, secret payloads and
article or customer content never reach logs, metrics or responses. Command
acceptance is not proof of playout; authoritative engine observations are.
Publication and recording state are security boundaries: only an explicitly
publishable state may produce a live effect, and non-publishable states fail
closed.

Assess purpose and evidence rather than the number of changed files or lines.
Bug fixes, meaningful tests that raise coverage, dependency repairs and
operational maintenance can serve this existing system without a new product
decision. New capabilities need repository documentation or linked acceptance
criteria that establish their need and boundaries. Production deployment is a
separate, explicitly authorized operation: merging to `main` runs the existing
deploy workflows, and a merge is not a deployment, health or on-air claim.

Ask gaulatti for a second opinion for a product-direction or authority decision:
for example a new public-destination provider, a change to who may start or stop
a broadcast, a new externally exposed control surface, multi-tenant hosting, or a
change to what is retained from a recording. Ordinary implementation uncertainty
and repairable bugs belong to automated investigation, not routine human code
review. Changes to review controls, coverage scope or exclusions, or this
purpose contract require explicit owner confirmation.

Every material capability and mechanism must independently score at least 80 for
fit, need and proportionality under Clouseau's shared protocol. A causal technical
finding at or above 70 blocks; unrelated features or good scores cannot average
away a defect. Integrity and review-completeness gates remain independent.

Tests must assert actual production behavior and failure outcomes. Reject
fabricated coverage, disabled tests, swallowed errors, unconditional assertions
and mocks that replace the behavior being claimed. Fault injection at an
external boundary (database, network, filesystem, LiveKit, AWS) is legitimate when
the real application contract and failure handling remain exercised. The gate
requires exactly 100% line and branch coverage of the application TypeScript and
JavaScript under `backend/src` for every contribution, including external forks,
and unloaded modules are measured. The React frontend (`frontend/`), the CDK package
(`infra/aws`) and `backend/scripts` are outside the exact-coverage gate for now;
their own tests still run where they exist. Narrowing or widening the gate is a
review-control change that requires owner confirmation.

A passing local Clouseau review may be reused only through a signed receipt from
an enrolled trusted workstation and the matching native GitHub author. CI must
independently verify current protected policy, exact head/base and engine content,
expiry, evidence and deterministic scores. All native tests, exact coverage and
branch protections remain mandatory. Clouseau owns the shared scoring,
investigation, repair bounds, evidence ledger, native approval and auto-merge;
this repository owns its purpose and real tests.

# Palazzo playback telemetry consumption

Alcantara's radio automation advances only from authoritative Palazzo playback
state. Estimated media duration never triggers song completion; it only
interpolates UI progress between authoritative updates.

## Ownership

- Programs of type `radio` and `both` each consume exactly one Palazzo
  instance through `PalazzoRadioTelemetryService`.
- Programs of type `tv` never consume Palazzo telemetry and keep their legacy
  estimated-duration engine behavior.
- Two radio-capable programs must not resolve to the same Palazzo instance
  identity. The second claimant is rejected with an `instance-conflict` and
  its radio leg is marked unavailable without affecting the first program.
- A Palazzo instance that changes identity under a program is rejected as an
  `instance-mismatch`, degrading only that program.

`PalazzoMachineClient` is the sole outbound transport. Song automation, manual
song controls, Flight and scene instants, scheduled bumpers, mixer reads and
writes, status hydration, SSE, polling, and startup recovery all use
`/v1/programs/{programId}` over the private broadcast network. The
single-program Palazzo appliance does not require a bearer token; network
isolation, Alcantara's URL allowlist, and exact program scoping are the trust
boundary. A repository-wide production caller must not use Palazzo's legacy
root playback routes.

## Correlation

- Every song, bumper, and manual playback command carries a unique
  `playbackRequestId` generated by Alcantara and sent to Palazzo.
- Palazzo event identity is `bootId + sequence`. The client deduplicates
  events per program, ignoring duplicates, older sequences, and events from
  superseded boots once a newer snapshot is accepted.
- A cursor gap aborts that SSE stream and reconciles the authenticated state
  snapshot before another lifecycle event can mutate the engine. Malformed and
  explicitly cross-program state/events are rejected.
- An event whose `type` Alcantara does not know (gaulatti/ariston#217) is
  skipped, never a reason to drop the stream: a well-formed frame of a new
  type is counted in
  `alcantara_palazzo_events_ignored_total{reason="unknown-type"}` (the label
  is that fixed reason, never the type), and when it is the next event of the
  accepted boot it advances the cursor so the known event after it is not a
  gap. A known event missing its required fields or a bad envelope is still
  malformed and reconnects the stream.
- `schemaVersion` is an integer and is the major version of the event and
  state contracts. Additive changes within major 1 (new fields, event types or
  enum values) carry no version bump, so they are the "minor" changes and are
  accepted by the rules here. An event whose `schemaVersion` is any other
  integer is skipped without reading any other field and counted in
  `alcantara_palazzo_events_ignored_total{reason="unsupported-version"}`; the
  stream stays up, and a later known event past its sequence is handled as a
  gap. A non-integer `schemaVersion` is malformed. A playback state of another
  major is still rejected.
- Within major 1, a state value Alcantara does not know degrades safely
  instead of rejecting the state (gaulatti/ariston#217): an unknown
  `availability` reads as `degraded`, an unknown `status` keeps the program's
  last accepted status (or `idle` before one, and on the operator state read),
  and an intro with an unknown `status` reads as no intro. An unknown
  `playout.next_withdrawn` reason keeps the event with reason `other` (the
  engine acts only on `not_ready`). Each is counted in
  `alcantara_palazzo_unknown_values_total{field}` with `field` one of
  `availability`, `status`, `intro-status` or `withdrawn-reason`, all exposed
  from 0; the unknown value is never a label. A missing, empty or mistyped
  value is still malformed.
- `track.started` with a matching request ID establishes authoritative start
  time and position.
- `track.ended` with a matching request ID advances the sequence exactly
  once. Duplicate, stale, cross-program, or mismatched-request events are
  no-ops.
- Assigned catalog intros use a deterministic child playback ID and the song
  request ID as `parentPlaybackId`. Matching `intro.started`, `intro.ended`,
  and `intro.failed` events update operator state only; they never advance,
  stop, or replace the parent song. Cross-program and mismatched-parent intro
  events are ignored.
- `playout.request_failed` (Palazzo 2d16d83 and later) for the active song
  that has not started marks it failed: it gets no as-run record, the control
  room's Radio desk shows the song, artist and reason (`timeout` or `other`;
  any other reason counts as `other`), and the sequence advances exactly once
  as at a natural end. An unknown request ID, a duplicate or a song already on
  air is ignored. An older Palazzo never sends the event, so nothing changes.
- Autoplay and Shuffle advance the in-memory playlist cursor to the next item
  after that authoritative end. Shuffle operates on its persisted randomized
  order, so it does not repeat an item before the current pass is exhausted.
  Looped playlists wrap; explicitly non-looped playlists publish stopped at
  their end. A missing song-sequence mode means autoplay, while an explicit
  `manual` mode remains an operator stop boundary.
- Play Next is a persisted FIFO queue of references to playable playlist item
  IDs. Duplicate song references are allowed as distinct queue entries. A
  normal track end advances and persists the underlying playlist cursor before
  the first queued command; queued track ends consume exactly their matching
  entry without advancing that cursor. When the queue drains, Autoplay and
  Shuffle resume from the saved successor while Manual publishes stopped.
  Alcantara persists a non-sensitive active marker and playback request ID
  before issuing a queued command, so restart adoption remains unambiguous even
  when the queued item is the same playlist item that was previously on air.
- When Alcantara restarts during playback, it adopts the inherited Palazzo
  track only when the authoritative audio URL identifies exactly one leaf in
  the configured sequence. Adoption preserves Palazzo's request ID, start time,
  and position, sends no competing play command, and advances from that exact
  leaf when its authoritative end arrives.
- An unknown URL, or a URL reused by multiple sequence leaves, remains foreign:
  Alcantara sends no command while it plays and does not guess a successor from
  its end event. When that foreign track ends, the engine reads Palazzo's
  current state (`GET .../playback/state`) and reconciles from it as from a
  snapshot: idle resumes normal automatic recovery. Explicit manual mode
  remains idle. (Palazzo sends a `snapshot` only when a stream connects, so
  waiting for one on a healthy connection stalled the rotation until the next
  reconnect: gaulatti/alcantara#230, ten hours on 2026-11-20.)
- **Playback watchdog (#230).** In autoplay or shuffle, every 10 s
  (`WATCHDOG_INTERVAL_MS`) the engine reads Palazzo's state. When Palazzo reports
  nothing on the air on reads at least 45 s apart (`NO_PLAYBACK_BOUND_MS`), the
  engine reconciles from that report: a song it still believes is on air is
  ended and the next one starts, and an empty engine starts the sequence.
  - **Nothing on the air** means `status` is `idle`, no intro is playing, the
    instant level is zero and `live.onAir` is false. An intro, an instant or a
    live show is never read as a stall.
  - **Why 45 s.** Palazzo's `status` reads `idle` while a commanded song is
    still loading, up to its request limit (`SONG_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`, 29 s by
    default). Every song command restarts the bound, so a load either starts or
    fails inside it. Production since 2026-11-19: the longest load was 1 s and
    the longest instant 11 s.
  - **It holds** (counted as `undecided`) while Palazzo reports itself
    `degraded`, or when its state has no `live` field (a Palazzo older than
    gaulatti/palazzo#48): with no way to rule a live show out, it starts no song
    under one.
  - It never acts in manual mode, while frozen, or while the stream is not
    reconciled, and never on elapsed time alone. A deploy candidate (#223) runs
    no watchdog.
- **After a failed song command (#230).** In autoplay or shuffle, a song
  command that Palazzo rejects no longer leaves the rotation quiet: after 2 s
  (`COMMAND_RETRY_BASE_MS`) the engine reads Palazzo's state and resumes from
  it, doubling the wait up to 30 s (`COMMAND_RETRY_MAX_MS`) while commands keep
  failing. Palazzo playing a song resets the wait. The retry stands down when a
  song or a command is already in flight, the engine is frozen, or the stream is
  not reconciled. Manual mode stays an operator boundary. On 2026-11-20 every
  Palazzo restart unfroze automation about 6 s before Palazzo could play, the
  first command failed, and the radio stayed silent until a person restarted
  the backend.

## Transports and failure behavior

Each program's client opens one SSE connection to the Palazzo
`/v1/programs/{programId}/playback/events` endpoint. Every connection begins with a complete
`snapshot` event; reconnections replay missed events via `Last-Event-ID`.
Palazzo deliberately removes URL-shaped fields from SSE. Alcantara accepts
URL-free lifecycle events by request ID and hydrates a redacted playing
snapshot from the private `/playback/state` endpoint before it reaches
the execution engine. This keeps media URLs out of the event stream without
mistaking a healthy stream for malformed telemetry.
A reconnect whose `Last-Event-ID` Palazzo can no longer replay (outside its
512-event window, or from another boot) gets a `replay.gap` event right after the
snapshot (palazzo#56; its data is `{reason: "cursor_not_in_replay", replayEvents}`,
and its id, boot and sequence are the snapshot's). Alcantara knows the type
(gaulatti/alcantara#240): the snapshot just hydrated and applied the current
state, so nothing more is fetched; the gap is counted under the existing
`alcantara_palazzo_events_ignored_total{reason="sequence-gap"}` and logged once at
warn level with the replay window size, the cursor stays at the snapshot, and the
event is not forwarded to the song engine, so what airs does not change. Its data
must be an object like every event's (otherwise `malformed`); a reason or field
it does not know is ignored. It is not shown on the console: it records that
events were missed, while the snapshot already carries the present state.
Current Palazzo preflight and playout-observation events advance the replay
cursor but are not forwarded into the song engine; only track, intro,
position, and level events may change Alcantara playback state. This prevents
an additive Palazzo event from being rejected or misclassified as a track end.
If Palazzo rejects or cannot accept a song command, Alcantara clears its
optimistic Radio playback, publishes stopped state, and increments the bounded
`alcantara_radio_track_transitions_total{result="command-failed"}` outcome; it
does not leave the console falsely on air or consume the queued entry. If the
failed command or an operator stop belonged to Play Next, Alcantara releases
the persisted playback claim while leaving that queue entry in place. If the
queue or the playlist cursor cannot be persisted at a queue transition,
Alcantara fails closed and publishes stopped instead of replaying a queue head
or falling through to a different playlist song.

- If SSE fails but `/v1/programs/{programId}/playback/state` responds, the client polls that endpoint
  (connection state `polling`) and reconciles snapshots while SSE reconnects
  with capped exponential backoff.
- If both transports are unavailable, the program's radio leg is marked
  `unavailable`, playback freezes, and Alcantara never advances, publishes a
  synthetic stop, or sends another song.
- Recovery reconciles the authoritative snapshot before any command resumes.
  An idle snapshot while a commanded song is active is treated as an
  authoritative track end and advances exactly once.

The `af97b09` invariant is preserved: autoplay, shuffle, and bumper handoffs
never publish an intermediate `stopped` now-playing state when a successor
becomes active. `stopped` is published only from an authoritative end with no
successor. Manual stop remains an explicit operator action and stays
distinguishable from appliance unavailability.

## Control surface

`GET /radio/:programId/palazzo-status` returns the connection state, instance
identity, telemetry freshness, and degraded flag per program. The radio panel
surfaces this live.

When a program of a radio type (`radio` or `both`) has no telemetry client the
endpoint answers an `unavailable` status instead of `null` (#257). A program
that is not of a radio type (a TV program, or an unknown id) has no engine and
keeps answering `null`, so no console shows an engine state for it. The
unavailable status is: `connection: "unavailable"`, `degraded: false`,
a plain-language `detail`, an empty `palazzoUrl` (a rejected URL is never
echoed), null instance and timestamps, and a bounded `reason`:
`not-configured` (no radio settings or no Palazzo URL), `disabled` (radio disabled in the program's settings),
`url-rejected` (the URL failed the allowlist when the client was started; see
`alcantara_palazzo_config_rejected_total`) or `deploy-candidate` (a deploy
candidate starts no telemetry). A configured, enabled program whose client has
not started yet answers `unavailable` with no `reason`. A live status carries no
`reason`. The set is additive: the console shows a known reason in plain words
("Engine unavailable: disabled in settings") and ignores an unknown, missing or
null one, which reads exactly as before, so an old console against this backend
(it reads only `connection`, `degraded` and `detail`) and this console against
an old backend (a `null` body) both keep working. The `console-fixture` state
`radio-not-configured` renders the reason. `radio_leg_status` and raw `palazzo_audio_levels` remain
available to realtime consumers; the same Palazzo levels are also normalized
into the existing `audio_meter_update` contract so the Radio desk's Song,
Audio clips, and Main meters show the appliance's actual output. Playback
updates retain the `telemetryStale` flag, and natural or manual off-air events
replace the stored playback state with `isPlaying: false` before fan-out.

The control console keeps `GET /program/:programId/events` SSE connected as its
authoritative feedback channel. Palazzo samples levels at 10 Hz by default and
Alcantara forwards each accepted sample immediately through that stream. The
control WebSocket connects only while SSE is unavailable; five-second HTTP
reconciliation runs only while both realtime channels are unavailable. A
connected but stalled fallback therefore cannot reduce the peak meter to
snapshot speed. The playback bar never estimates an on-air state from playlist
timing: it shows progress only from backend playback feedback and labels that
feedback as live or stale.

The Radio desk exposes the live Song, Audio clips / bumpers, and Main mixer
channels. Changes persist in the program audio bus and are synchronously sent
to Palazzo's Liquidsoap mixer. The shared instant bus controls both manually
triggered instants and scheduled bumpers; each instant's own volume is then
multiplied by that bus and the main output gain. Bumper settings persist
`bumperEnabled`, `bumperInterval`, `bumperInstantIds`, and `bumperMode`; invalid
intervals, IDs, or modes fail visibly instead of being dropped.

The same desk exposes Play Next above the normal playlist. Operators add a
playlist row without interrupting the current song, inspect FIFO order, remove
entries, and reorder entries that have not started. Queue mutations use the
protected `POST`, `PUT`, and `DELETE /program/:programId/song-queue` routes.
Public audio-bus snapshots include `songQueue`; `song_queue_update` carries
live queue changes and shares the audio-bus version watermark. Queue entries
are removed only after a matching authoritative `track.ended` event.

Playlist leaves may carry `highRotation: true`; the protected audio-bus update
accepts at most 12 such leaves. In Autoplay and Shuffle, Alcantara owns their
cadence: one High Rotation opportunity opens every 30 minutes and selects the
least recently played eligible favorite. Authoritative `track.started` events
are recorded in the additive `ProgramState.songRotation` state so restarts do
not reset the distribution. The 48 daily opportunities are shared evenly among
the current favorites, so every configured favorite receives at least four
plays per day. The repeat gap is `favorite count / 2` hours: 12 favorites play
four times each with six-hour spacing, while four favorites play 12 times each
with two-hour spacing. Least-recently-played selection avoids repeating a song
before the rest of the pool. Play Next and manual takes retain operator
priority; a favorite played through either path contributes to the persisted
history and is moved behind less-recently-played favorites.

Automation settings, Palazzo URL, bumper eligibility, and now-playing consumers
live at `/radio-settings`; they are deliberately separate from live playout.
A now-playing consumer URL must use https, and every delivery follows the
outbound-request policy in [outbound-requests.md](outbound-requests.md).
For a `both` program, the TV control adds a radio-leg status rail. Scene actions
remain TV-only while Songs and Audio clips flow through the shared program mix.

The playback bar's Shuffle action persists a newly randomized playlist order,
anchors the authoritative current track at the front, and remains in the
visible `shuffle` mode while advancing through every remaining item once before
loop behavior applies. It does not reset the current track's start time or
change the loop setting while feedback says that track is playing. Activating
Shuffle from idle selects the first shuffled item and starts a fresh playback
clock, including after a non-looped playlist has ended. Manual, Autoplay, and Shuffle expose mutually
exclusive pressed states; Loop exposes an independent on/off pressed state.

Previous, Play/Advance, Stop, and Next each take one authoritative action.
Play starts the selected item rather than skipping it, Advance and Next do not
wrap when Loop is off, and Stop uses the program off-air endpoint without a
duplicate sequence write. An idle automatic selection starts through the
persisted sequence update alone, avoiding a second manual Palazzo command.

## Private machine configuration

The browser calls Alcantara only and never receives direct Palazzo access.
Local Compose supplies `PALAZZO_ALLOWED_URLS=http://palazzo:3100`; Palazzo must
be reachable on the local/private Docker network for radio integration tests.
The single-host, single-program Palazzo API has no bearer credential.

Production sets only the bootstrap `ALCANTARA_CONFIG_SECRET_ID` and AWS region.
Before Nest constructs `AppModule` or any Palazzo client, Alcantara reads that
Secrets Manager JSON and selects only these scalar fields:

```json
{
  "palazzoAllowedUrls": "http://palazzo:3100",
  "alanaControlToken": "replace-in-secrets-manager",
  "alanaControlUrl": "http://alana:8080",
  "externalSourceConfigCurrentVersion": "1",
  "externalSourceConfigKeys": "{\"1\":\"base64-encoded-32-byte-root\"}"
}
```

Retrieval failure, malformed values, or any missing field fails startup. There
is no plaintext production Alana token or encryption-key environment fallback
when the Secrets Manager bootstrap is configured. The runtime IAM identity
needs only `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` for this one Alcantara configuration
secret (plus `kms:Decrypt` only when a customer-managed key requires it).

Deployment requires Palazzo to be running on the private `broadcast-control`
network and supplies the fixed private
`PALAZZO_ALLOWED_URLS=http://palazzo:3100`. Secrets Manager remains the
preferred bootstrap for the allowlist and all remaining private configuration;
if configuration does not validate, deployment leaves the current backend
untouched. `palazzoAllowedUrls` is enforced before every machine call so an
operator-editable `palazzoUrl` cannot redirect radio control outside the
approved private origin.

## Metrics

`GET /metrics` exposes Prometheus text format 0.0.4. The route is public only to
Alcantara's application authorization guard so that a dedicated scraper can
reach it; `MetricsTokenGuard` independently requires a bearer credential read
from `METRICS_TOKEN_FILE` (default
`/run/secrets/alcantara-metrics-token`). Missing credentials fail closed with
`503`; absent or incorrect bearer values return `401`. Never publish or pass the
credential as a build argument or ordinary environment value.

Deployment provisioning: the production secret `broadcast/production/config`
carries a `metrics_bearer_token` field (ignored by the runtime secret contract).
After the candidate check passes and before the running backend is stopped,
`deploy/cumulus.sh` runs `scripts/print-metrics-token.mjs` inside the new image.
The script writes only the trimmed field to stdout; the deploy pipes it into a
root-owned `0400` file (`/etc/alcantara/metrics-token`), which is mounted
read-only at `/run/secrets/alcantara-metrics-token` on the live backend with
`METRICS_TOKEN_FILE` set. The script never logs the token or the secret payload,
and a missing, blank or non-string field, or an unreadable secret, fails the
deploy before the live backend is touched. The deploy candidate does not get the
mount: its health check calls `GET /` and never `/metrics`. Rotate by changing
the secret field and redeploying, then updating the scraper's token file.
The on-premises workflow path (`.github/workflows/backend-deploy.yml`) is wired
separately.

Boundary: the provisioning itself adds no metric family or label. The
scrape surface is the backend's HTTP port with two routes behind the same
`MetricsTokenGuard` (`GET /metrics` and `GET /metrics/palazzo`, below), the
bearer value never appears in metric labels, logs, build arguments or the
container environment, and the Prometheus scrape job and its credential file
belong to the observability repository (milano).

### Rejected Palazzo configuration (#257)

`alcantara_palazzo_config_rejected_total` (no labels) counts Palazzo URLs the
allowlist rejected when a program's telemetry client was started, at startup or
when its radio settings change. It increments once per rejection, never when the
status is read. A program whose URL is rejected has no engine until its settings
change; its status says `url-rejected`. The URL is neither a label nor part of
the log line (`Palazzo URL configuration rejected for <program>`).

### Degraded engine paths (#237)

`alcantara_radio_engine_degraded_total{site}` counts the engine paths that carry
on in a degraded way instead of failing. Each one also logs one warning naming
the program and the error class, never the error message:

- `telemetry_state`: a resync could not read Palazzo's state (`Resync could not
  read Palazzo state for <program> (<class>)`); the resync then records
  `unavailable`.
- `bumper_settings`: the radio settings could not be read when an announced
  bumper ended, so the bumper sequence stays where it was.
- `bumper_attempt`: the bumper path failed before its send, for example
  because the settings or the instant could not be read. No spot plays.
- `radio_settings_missing`: a song command for a program without radio
  settings, answered `ok: false` (`Radio settings missing for program <id>`).

Every site is rendered from zero.

### Engine resyncs (#230)

`alcantara_radio_engine_resyncs_total{trigger,result}` counts the times the song
engine read Palazzo's state itself. `trigger` is `foreign_ended` (a foreign
track ended), `watchdog` (Palazzo reported nothing on the air past the bound)
or `command_failed` (the retry after a failed song command). `result` is
`resumed` (Palazzo was idle and the engine reconciled from it, which for the
watchdog means it commanded a song or advanced past an end),
`resumed_no_command` (watchdog only, gaulatti/alcantara#233: the watchdog
resumed but nothing was commanded or advanced; the log line `Watchdog resume
commanded nothing on <program>: <reason>` names `held_song`, `queue_blocked`,
`clocked_log`, `foreign_track` or `no_successor`), `playing` (Palazzo was
playing; nothing to do), `unavailable` (no state could be read) or `undecided`
(the watchdog held: Palazzo degraded or not reporting its live input). All
thirteen series are always present. Any `watchdog,resumed_no_command` is worth
paging on: the radio is silent and the engine's recovery did nothing (the
2026-11-21 00:28Z stall looked like a healthy `resumed`). A rising `watchdog,resumed` or `command_failed,resumed` means the
rotation stalled and recovered on its own; a rising `unavailable` means the
engine could not read Palazzo; a steady `watchdog,undecided` means the watchdog
cannot act (check Palazzo's version and availability).

### Palazzo metrics passthrough

`GET /metrics/palazzo` lets the single authenticated scrape reach Palazzo's own
`/metrics` without publishing Palazzo. It is authenticated by the metrics token
exactly like `GET /metrics` (`503` credential unavailable, `401` absent or wrong
bearer; Palazzo is never contacted in those cases). The outbound request is a
fixed `GET <origin>/metrics`, where the origin is the one entry of the existing
`PALAZZO_ALLOWED_URLS` (no new variable, no fallback host; zero, several or an
invalid entry fail closed and log one warning without the value). Nothing from
the incoming request is used: the scrape bearer is never forwarded, redirects
are not followed (a redirect counts as a failure), and the whole exchange,
including the body read, has a 2 second budget and a 5 MiB body cap. A `200`
returns Palazzo's text unchanged as `text/plain; version=0.0.4`. Palazzo
unreachable, timing out, answering non-2xx, or answering an oversized body
returns `502` with an empty body, so the scrape never hangs.

| Metric family                                       | Bounded labels                                       | Operational meaning                         |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `alcantara_palazzo_metrics_scrape_total`            | `result`: `ok`, `unavailable`, `timeout`, `too_large`, `error` | Outcome of each passthrough (`unavailable`: unconfigured or connection failure; `error`: non-2xx, redirect or body read failure) |
| `alcantara_palazzo_metrics_scrape_duration_seconds` | none                                                 | Wall time of each passthrough, up to the 2 s budget |

The HTTP metrics label the route as the existing `metrics` group.

| Metric family                                  | Bounded labels                      | Operational meaning                            |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `alcantara_service_info`                       | `service`, `runtime`, `version`     | Service/build identity                         |
| `alcantara_process_*`, `alcantara_nodejs_*`    | prom-client runtime labels only     | Node.js and process health                     |

## Song analysis drop metric

`alcantara_radio_analysis_dropped_total{result}` counts analysis-derived segue or loudness that the radio service left off a song command or next-song announcement, with `segueMode` on, because Palazzo would reject it or because the song had no analysis to send. The song still plays without the dropped group. `result` is one of `segue-invalid` (cue, fade or overlap values outside Palazzo's bounds), `segue-beyond-duration` (cue-out after the song's duration), `segue-edge-bound` (one cue edge would trim more than 10 s, or is negative or not finite; the other edge is still sent, gaulatti/alcantara#234), `loudness-invalid` (integrated loudness outside -70 to 0 LUFS, true peak above +6 dBTP, or a non-finite value), `ambiguous-match` (the command named no song and more than one song shares its audio URL, so no analysis was applied), or, for a song sent with no analysis at all (gaulatti/alcantara#255): `no-asset` (no library song matches, or the song has no media asset), `not-analyzed` (the asset's analysis is missing, pending or failed) or `lookup-failed` (the song or analysis lookup itself failed). In these last three cases the song is still sent, unchanged, without segue or loudness normalization. The counter counts commands, not aired songs: the same check runs for a song command and for a next-song announcement, so one song can count twice (announced, then commanded after a refused or replaced announcement), and a withdrawn announcement counts a song that never aired. Read it as an upper bound on songs sent without analysis, by reason. Not counted here: an analysis that succeeded but measured no loudness (it airs without normalization; its cue group is counted as `none` only when it also has no cues). Every result is exported at 0 from start-up. Labels never include songs, URLs or program IDs. Each song with a drop is also logged once as `radio.song_analysis_dropped`. See [program-playout.md](program-playout.md).

`alcantara_radio_cue_groups_total{shape}` counts the cue groups the radio service resolved for a song command or a next-song announcement (gaulatti/alcantara#234):
- `both`: both edges measured;
- `head_filled`: only the tail was measured, cue-in sent as 0;
- `tail_filled`: only the head was measured, cue-out sent as the duration;
- `none`: no edge left to trim, or the group was dropped.

A caller-supplied segue is not counted. A song is counted once per command or announcement, so a re-announced song counts again.

Contract: gaulatti/palazzo#40 §5.

  - `intro`;

    `Next song not announced on <program>: <reason> (<detail>)` says which;
  - `queue_head_active`: the queue head is already on air;
  - `not_autoplay`;
  - `unsupported`: a 404 Palazzo;
  - `superseded`: the song changed while the successor was worked out;
  - `refused`: Palazzo did not accept the announcement.

  A handoff counted `command` with no skip for its song had its announcement
